record.paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
record.context_brief: energy identity for scalar curvature measures
record.original_question: Consider a sequence of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converging to (X, d, x), with Ric_j ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Let R_j dvol_{g_j} converge as measures on X. On the part of X where tangent cones are uniquely of the form R^(n−2) × C(S^1_{r_x}), with radius function r_x, must the scalar-curvature measures satisfy the energy-identity decomposition R_j dvol_{g_j} → R_X H^n + 2 θ_x H^{n−1}_Σ + 2π(1 − r_x) H^{n−2}_S, where R_X is a locally L^1 function bounded below, Σ is an (n−1)-rectifiable set with θ_x ≤ 1, and the final term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X)?

evidence.quote: To be precise recall from Theorem 2.12 that away from a set of n − 2 measure zero there is a radius function rx such that at any x in the domain we have that the tangent cone at x is unique and isometric to Rn−2 × C(S1rx).

Conjecture 2.20 (energy identity). Let (Mnj, gj, xj) → (X, d, x) satisfy Ricj ≥ −λ and the noncollapsing condition Vol(B1(xj)) ≥ v > 0, then as measures the scalar curvature converges Rj dvj → RXHn + 2θxHn−1Σ + 2π(1 − rx)Hn−2S, where RX : X → R is a locally L1 function which is bounded from below, Σ is an n−1 rectifiable set with θx ≤ 1, and 2π(1−rx)Hn−2S is an n−2-rectifiable measure supported on the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 3, and let (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) be a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian manifolds satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound Ric_{g_j} ≥ −λ for some constant λ ≥ 0, together with the noncollapsing condition Vol_{g_j}(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Assume (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space (X, d, x), and that the scalar curvature measures R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} converge as Radon measures on X to some limit measure μ.

It is known that on X there exists a subset of full (n−2)-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the top singular stratum on which the tangent cone at each point y is unique and isometric to ℝ^{n−2} × C(S^1_{r_y}), where C(S^1_r) denotes the metric cone over a circle of length 2πr and r_y ∈ (0,1] is the corresponding radius (so 2π(1 − r_y) is the cone angle defect). Denote this radius function by r_·.

Prove or disprove the following energy-identity decomposition: as measures on X,
   R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} ⟶ R_X · 𝓗^n + 2 θ · 𝓗^{n−1}⌞Σ + 2π(1 − r_·) · 𝓗^{n−2}⌞S,
where:
 (i) R_X : X → ℝ is locally integrable with respect to 𝓗^n and bounded below;
 (ii) Σ ⊂ X is an (n−1)-rectifiable set and θ : Σ → (0, 1] is a Borel density satisfying θ ≤ 1;
 (iii) S is the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X), the third term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on S, and r_· is the radius function described above.
artifact.status_search_result: No search result indicates a proof of this energy-identity decomposition for scalar curvature measures on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. The conjecture remains stated as an open problem; related results (e.g., L^2 curvature bounds, structure of singular strata, energy identities for Yang–Mills) are known but do not establish this specific scalar-curvature energy identity. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Aaron Naber CV
status_evidence.snippet: Lists publications on structure theory of metric-measure spaces with lower Ricci curvature bounds; no entry establishing the scalar-curvature energy identity for Ricci limits.
status_evidence.claim: No publication resolving the conjectured energy identity is listed.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds on Ricci curvature and quantitative behavior of singular sets
status_evidence.snippet: Cheeger–Naber establish rectifiability of singular strata of noncollapsed Ricci limits, but do not establish the proposed scalar curvature energy-identity decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on singular strata exist but the energy identity is not proven.
